extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing manuscripts for Communications in Mathematical Physics (mathematical physicists and related researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting manuscripts to the journal Communications in Mathematical Physics, including formatting, ethical requirements, data and figure preparation, authorship, declarations, and post-acceptance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and simultaneous submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a manuscript implies: that the work described has not been published before; that it is not under consideration for publication anywhere else; that its publication has been approved by all co-authors, if any, as well as by the responsible authorities ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The publisher will not be held legally responsible should there be any claims for compensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions for previously published material
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors wishing to include figures, tables, or text passages that have already been published elsewhere are required to obtain permission from the copyright owner(s) for both the print and online format and to include evidence that such permission has been granted when submitting their papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any material received without such evidence will be assumed to originate from the authors; some publishers may not grant electronic rights for free and Springer will not refund permission costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online submission procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Please follow the hyperlink 'Submit manuscript' and upload all of your manuscript files following the instructions given on the screen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide editable source files at all stages
rubrics_metrics.description: Please ensure you provide all relevant editable source files at every submission and revision. Failing to submit a complete set of editable source files will result in your article not being considered for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For your manuscript text please always submit in common word processing formats such as .docx or LaTeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial submission format (concise guideline)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the first (initial) submission, please upload a pdf file of your manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You will be asked to submit the complete set editable LATEX source files at later stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title page: title
rubrics_metrics.description: The title should be concise and informative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title page: author information
rubrics_metrics.description: The name(s) of the author(s); the affiliation(s) of the author(s), i.e. institution, (department), city, (state), country; a clear indication and an active e-mail address of the corresponding author; If available, the 16-digit ORCID of the author(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If address information is provided with the affiliation(s) it will also be published. For temporarily unaffiliated authors only city and country of residence are captured, not e-mail unless requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative AI / LLMs authorship policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Large Language Models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT, do not currently satisfy our authorship criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of an LLM should be properly documented in the Methods section (or suitable alternative). AI-assisted copy editing (readability/style/grammar fixes) does not need to be declared. There must be human accountability for the final version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract length and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Please provide an abstract of 150 to 250 words. The abstract should not contain any undefined abbreviations or unspecified references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements and Declarations required
rubrics_metrics.description: The following statements should be included under the heading 'Statements and Declarations' for inclusion in the published paper. Please note that submissions that do not include relevant declarations will be returned as incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competing Interests and other relevant declarations must appear; see specific sections for examples of wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX template recommendation and source submission
rubrics_metrics.description: For LaTeX submissions we encourage authors to use the Springer Nature LaTeX template when preparing a submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The submission should include the original source (including all style files and figures) and a PDF version of the compiled output. Use of the Springer macro package is optional. Word files are also accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings format
rubrics_metrics.description: Please use the decimal system of headings with no more than three levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated guidance: headings should follow decimal system throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviations should be defined at first mention and used consistently thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnotes can be used to give additional information, which may include the citation of a reference included in the reference list. They should not consist solely of a reference citation, and they should never include the bibliographic details of a reference. They should also not contain any figures or tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes to the text are numbered consecutively; those to tables should be indicated by superscript lower-case letters (or asterisks for significance values and other statistical data). Footnotes to the title or the authors of the article are not given reference symbols. Always use footnotes instead of endnotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgments placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgments of people, grants, funds, etc. should be placed in a separate section on the title page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The names of funding organizations should be written in full.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific notation style
rubrics_metrics.description: Please use the standard mathematical notation for formulae, symbols etc.: Italic for single letters that denote mathematical constants, variables, and unknown quantities; Roman/upright for numerals, operators, and punctuation, and commonly defined functions or abbreviations; Bold for vectors, tensors, and matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: cos, det, e or exp, lim, log, max, min, sin, tan, d (for derivative).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation style in text
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference citations in the text should be identified by numbers in square brackets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided for single and ranges [1-3, 7].

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference list content and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: The list of references should only include works that are cited in the text and that have been published or accepted for publication. Personal communications and unpublished works should only be mentioned in the text. The entries in the list should be numbered consecutively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If available, always include DOIs as full DOI links. Use standard journal abbreviations per ISSN LTWA; if unsure use full journal title. Examples provided for journal article, article by DOI, book, book chapter, online document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables: numbering and caption
rubrics_metrics.description: All tables are to be numbered using Arabic numerals. Tables should always be cited in text in consecutive numerical order. For each table, please supply a table caption (title) explaining the components of the table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify any previously published material by giving the original source in the form of a reference at the end of the table caption. Footnotes to tables indicated by superscript lower-case letters (or asterisks) and included beneath the table body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic figure submission and preferred formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply all figures electronically. Indicate what graphics program was used to create the artwork. For vector graphics, the preferred format is EPS; for halftones, please use TIFF format. MSOffice files are also acceptable. Vector graphics containing fonts must have the fonts embedded in the files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name figure files with 'Fig' and the figure number, e.g., Fig1.eps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line art requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition: Black and white graphic with no shading. Do not use faint lines and/or lettering and check that all lines and lettering within the figures are legible at final size. All lines should be at least 0.1 mm (0.3 pt) wide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scanned line drawings and line drawings in bitmap format should have a minimum resolution of 1200 dpi. Vector graphics containing fonts must have the fonts embedded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Halftone art requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition: Photographs, drawings, or paintings with fine shading, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any magnification is used in the photographs, indicate this by using scale bars within the figures themselves. Halftones should have a minimum resolution of 300 dpi.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination artwork resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition: a combination of halftone and line art, e.g., halftones containing line drawing, extensive lettering, color diagrams, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combination artwork should have a minimum resolution of 600 dpi.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color art guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Color art is free of charge for online publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If black and white will be shown in the print version, make sure that the main information will still be visible. Do not refer to color in captions if print version is black-and-white. Color illustrations should be submitted as RGB (8 bits per channel).

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure lettering and font guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: To add lettering, it is best to use Helvetica or Arial (sans serif fonts). Keep lettering consistently sized throughout your final-sized artwork, usually about 2–3 mm (8–12 pt). Variance of type size within an illustration should be minimal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid effects such as shading, outline letters, etc. Do not include titles or captions within your illustrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure numbering and figure parts
rubrics_metrics.description: All figures are to be numbered using Arabic numerals. Figures should always be cited in text in consecutive numerical order. Figure parts should be denoted by lowercase letters (a, b, c, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an appendix appears in your article and it contains one or more figures, continue the consecutive numbering of the main text. Figures in online appendices (Supplementary Information) should be numbered separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure captions formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Each figure should have a concise caption describing accurately what the figure depicts. Include the captions in the text file of the manuscript, not in the figure file. Figure captions begin with the term Fig. in bold type, followed by the figure number, also in bold type. No punctuation is to be included after the number, nor is any punctuation to be placed at the end of the caption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify all elements found in the figure in the figure caption; and use boxes, circles, etc., as coordinate points in graphs. Identify previously published material by giving the original source in the form of a reference citation at the end of the figure caption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure placement and sizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should be submitted within the body of the text. Only if the file size of the manuscript causes problems in uploading it, the large figures should be submitted separately from the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing your figures, size figures to fit in the column width. Specific width/height dimensions provided for large- and small-sized journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility of figures
rubrics_metrics.description: All figures have descriptive captions (blind users could then use a text-to-speech software or a text-to-Braille hardware). Patterns are used instead of or in addition to colors for conveying information (colorblind users would then be able to distinguish the visual elements). Any figure lettering has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative AI images compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Please check Springer’s policy on generative AI images and make sure your work adheres to the principles described therein.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary Information: accepted types and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer accepts electronic multimedia files (animations, movies, audio, etc.) and other supplementary files to be published online along with an article or a book chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply all supplementary material in standard file formats and include article title, journal name, author names; affiliation and e-mail address of the corresponding author in each file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary Information: file format specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Audio, Video, and Animations: Aspect ratio 16:9 or 4:3; Maximum file size 2 GB; Minimum video duration 1 sec; Supported file formats: avi, wmv, mp4, mov, m2p, mp2, mpg, mpeg, flv, mxf, mts, m4v, 3gp. Text and Presentations: submit in PDF; Spreadsheets: .csv or .xlsx; Specialized formats such as .pdb, .wrl, .nb, and .tex can also be supplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To accommodate user downloads, larger files may require long download times; collect multiple files in .zip or .gz if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary Information: numbering, captions, references
rubrics_metrics.description: If supplying any supplementary material, the text must make specific mention of the material as a citation, similar to that of figures and tables. Refer to the supplementary files as 'Online Resource', e.g., '... as shown in the animation (Online Resource 3)'. Name the files consecutively, e.g. 'ESM_3.mpg', 'ESM_4.pdf'. For each supplementary material, please supply a concise caption describing the content of the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplementary Information will be published as received from the author without any conversion, editing, or reformatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary Information accessibility and safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure the manuscript contains a descriptive caption for each supplementary material. Video files do not contain anything that flashes more than three times per second (so that users prone to seizures caused by such effects are not put at risk).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generative AI images: follow Springer policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research data policy: data availability statement required
rubrics_metrics.description: This journal follows Springer Nature research data policy. Sharing of all relevant research data is strongly encouraged and authors must add a Data Availability Statement to original research articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data availability statements should explain how to access data supporting the results including links/citations to archived datasets; guidance and examples are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research data: when data cannot be shared
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is not possible to share research data publicly, for instance when individual privacy could be compromised, this statement should describe how data can be accessed and any conditions for reuse. Participant consent should be obtained and documented prior to data collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the minimal dataset necessary to interpret and replicate findings; see guidance on sensitive data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data repositories and recommended practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are strongly encouraged to deposit their supporting data in a publicly available repository. We recommend the use of discipline-specific repositories where available. For a number of data types, submission to specific public repositories is mandatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journal encourages making research data available under open licences that permit reuse; ensure you have necessary rights to share any data that you deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data citation format
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal recommends that authors cite any publicly available data on which the conclusions of the paper rely. Data citations should include a persistent identifier (such as a DOI), should be included in the reference list using the minimum information recommended by DataCite (Dataset Creator, Dataset Title, Publisher [repository], Publication Year, Identifier) and follow journal style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further guidance on citing datasets is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research data and peer review anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: If the journal uses double-anonymous peer review and you are providing reviewers with access to your data, it is strongly suggested that the authorship in the data is also anonymised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data repositories can assist with anonymisation and/or create masked links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for data policy compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors who need help understanding data sharing policy, finding a suitable repository, or organising and sharing research data can consult the Research Data Helpdesk for guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See FAQ page for more information on Springer Nature's research data policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing services optionality
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting your work in a well-structured manuscript and in well-written English gives it its best chance for editors and reviewers to understand it and evaluate it fairly. Springer Nature Author Services can help with English language editing, developmental comments, manuscript formatting, figure preparation, translation, and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using these tools is not a requirement for publication, nor does it imply or guarantee acceptance or peer review selection. Free Grammar Check tool available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical responsibilities and COPE adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: This journal is committed to upholding the integrity of the scientific record. As a member of COPE the journal will follow COPE guidelines on how to deal with potential acts of misconduct. Authors should refrain from misrepresenting research results which could damage trust in the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining integrity is helped by following rules of good scientific practice listed (no simultaneous submission, originality, no salami-slicing, proper citation, avoid fabrication/falsification, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Good scientific practice: no salami-slicing and related rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The submitted work should be original and should not have been published elsewhere in any form or language (partially or in full), unless the new work concerns an expansion of previous work. A single study should not be split up into several parts to increase the quantity of submissions ('salami-slicing/publishing').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concurrent or secondary publication is sometimes justifiable provided certain conditions (e.g., translations) are met; provide transparency on re-use to avoid text-recycling concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and image integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Results should be presented clearly, honestly, and without fabrication, falsification or inappropriate data manipulation (including image based manipulation). Authors should adhere to discipline-specific rules for acquiring, selecting and processing data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon request authors should be prepared to send relevant documentation or data to verify validity (raw data, samples, records). Sensitive/confidential data excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism and attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: No data, text, or theories by others are presented as if they were the author’s own ('plagiarism'). Proper acknowledgements must be given (including near verbatim material, summarized/paraphrased material), quotation marks for verbatim copying, and permissions secured for copyrighted material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important note: the journal may use software to screen for plagiarism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual-use and potentially harmful research
rubrics_metrics.description: Research that may be misapplied to pose a threat to public health or national security should be clearly identified in the manuscript (e.g., dual use of research).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include creation of harmful biological agents, disruption of vaccine immunity, unusual hazards in chemical use, weaponization of research/technology; such research should be identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship correctness at submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are strongly advised to ensure the author group, the Corresponding Author, and the order of authors are all correct at submission. Adding and/or deleting authors during the revision stages is generally not permitted, but in some cases may be warranted. Changes to authorship cannot be made after acceptance of a manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Names will be published exactly as they appear on the accepted submission; make sure names and affiliations are present and correctly spelled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of suspected misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is suspicion of misbehavior or alleged fraud the Journal and/or Publisher will carry out an investigation following COPE guidelines. Depending on the situation, measures may include rejection, erratum/correction, expression of concern, or retraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reason will be given in the published erratum/correction or retraction note. The author's institution may be informed. Notice of suspected transgression may be included in bibliographic record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to correct fundamental errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors have an obligation to correct mistakes once they discover a significant error or inaccuracy in their published article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the journal and explain how the error impacts the article; correction method (correction or retraction) depends on nature of error. Retraction notes should provide transparency about impacted parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggesting and excluding reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are welcome to suggest suitable reviewers and/or request the exclusion of certain individuals when they submit their manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When suggesting reviewers, ensure they are totally independent and not connected to the work. Recommend a mix of reviewers from different countries and institutions. Provide institutional email or other verifiable identity. The Journal may not use suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship criteria (recommended/adapted from ICMJE)
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors whose names appear on the submission: 1) made substantial contributions to conception/design, data acquisition/analysis/interpretation, or creation of new software; 2) drafted or revised critically for important intellectual content; 3) approved the version to be published; and 4) agree to be accountable for all aspects of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations based on/adapted from ICMJE and other published guidance; publisher does not prescribe exact contributions but recommends adherence to field-specific guidelines where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosures and declarations to include
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors are requested to include information regarding sources of funding, financial or non-financial interests, study-specific approval by the appropriate ethics committee for research involving humans and/or animals, informed consent if research involved human participants, and a statement on welfare of animals if the research involved animals (as appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision whether such information should be included depends on scope of journal and article; work with public health implications should include appropriate disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data transparency obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors are requested to make sure that all data and materials as well as software application or custom code support their published claims and comply with field standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals may have individual policies on sharing research data in concordance with disciplinary norms and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corresponding Author responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: One author is assigned as Corresponding Author and acts on behalf of all co-authors and ensures that questions related to the accuracy or integrity of any part of the work are appropriately addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibilities include ensuring all listed authors have approved the manuscript and names/order; managing communication between Journal and co-authors; providing transparency on re-use of material; making sure disclosures/declarations and data statements from all authors are included. Management of communication may be delegated to Contact or Submitting Author but Corresponding Author must be clearly indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author contributions statements and CRediT
rubrics_metrics.description: In absence of specific instructions and where possible, the Publisher recommends authors include contribution statements specifying the contribution of every author to promote transparency. Examples include free-text statements and CRediT taxonomy roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For review articles include who had the idea, who performed literature search and data analysis, who drafted or revised. For student dissertation-based articles student is usually listed as principal author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliation and address conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary affiliation for each author should be the institution where the majority of their work was done. If an author has subsequently moved, the current address may additionally be stated. Addresses will not be updated or changed after publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes to authorship policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are strongly advised to ensure the correct author group, the Corresponding Author, and the order of authors at submission. Changes of authorship (adding/deleting authors or changes in sequence) are not accepted after acceptance of a manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding/deleting authors at revision stage are generally not permitted but may be warranted in some cases; reasons must be explained and approval of change during revision is at Editor-in-Chief discretion. Author names will be published exactly as they appear on accepted submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author identification recommendation (ORCID)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are recommended to use their ORCID ID when submitting an article for consideration or acquire an ORCID ID via the submission process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deceased or incapacitated authors
rubrics_metrics.description: For cases in which a co-author dies or is incapacitated during the writing, submission, or peer-review process, and the co-authors feel it is appropriate to include the author, co-authors should obtain approval from a (legal) representative which could be a direct relative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship disputes resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of an authorship dispute during peer review or after acceptance and publication, the Journal will not be in a position to investigate or adjudicate. Authors will be asked to resolve the dispute themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors are unable to resolve the dispute the Journal reserves the right to withdraw a manuscript from the editorial process or, in case of a published paper, raise the issue with the authors’ institution(s) and abide by its guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of journal communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should treat all communication with the Journal as confidential which includes correspondence with Editors-in-Chief and/or Handling Editors and reviewers’ reports unless explicit consent has been received to share information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are requested to disclose interests that are directly or indirectly related to the work submitted for publication. Interests within the last 3 years of beginning the work should be reported. Interests outside the 3-year time frame must be disclosed if they could reasonably be perceived as influencing the submitted work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure is intended to provide transparency and assist readers in judging potential bias. Editors/Editorial Board Members must declare competing interests and may be excluded from handling manuscripts where a competing interest exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of interests to consider
rubrics_metrics.description: Interests include funding (research grants, support), employment (recent/present/anticipated), financial interests (stocks, consultancy fees, patents), and non-financial interests (positions on boards, consulting, expert witness, mentoring relationships).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No strict threshold for financial interest; a practical guideline: 'Any undeclared financial interest that could embarrass the author were it to become publicly known after the work was published.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Article types requiring disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary research articles require a disclosure statement. Review articles present an expert synthesis and therefore require a disclosure statement. Other article types such as editorials, book reviews, comments may, dependent on content, require a disclosure statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unclear whether an article type requires disclosure contact the Editor-in-Chief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of Declarations placement
rubrics_metrics.description: The above (funding, competing interests, ethics approval, consent, data/material/code availability, authors’ contributions) should be summarized in a statement and placed in a 'Declarations' section before the reference list under a heading of 'Funding' and/or 'Competing interests'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When all authors have the same (or no) conflicts a single blanket statement is sufficient. Examples of wording for various funding/competing interest scenarios are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: After acceptance: typesetting and proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon acceptance, your article will be exported to Production to undergo typesetting. Shortly after this you will receive two e-mails: one to confirm affiliation, choose publishing model, arrange rights and payment; a second with a link to your article’s proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The purpose of the proof is to check for typesetting or conversion errors and completeness/accuracy of text/tables/figures. Substantial changes in content are not allowed without Editor approval. After online publication further changes possible only via an Erratum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article publishing agreement / copyright
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on the ownership of the journal and its policies, you will either grant the Publisher an exclusive licence to publish the article or will be asked to transfer copyright of the article to the Publisher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offprints and color charges after acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Offprints can be ordered by the corresponding author. Online publication of color illustrations is free of charge. For color in the print version, authors will be expected to make a contribution towards the extra costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online First publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The article will be published online after receipt of the corrected proofs. This is the official first publication citable with the DOI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After release of the printed version, the paper can also be cited by issue and page numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Choice (open access) option
rubrics_metrics.description: Open Choice allows you to publish open access in more than 1850 Springer Nature journals, making your research more visible and accessible immediately on publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article processing charges vary by journal; benefits and funding/support pages linked; OA articles remain with author copyright under a Creative Commons license on opting for Open Choice.
